metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code with deployable entry point (server.js with app.listen(8080)), Dockerfile, and Kubernetes manifests present. Single-service application.
metadata.archetype_justification: Read-heavy data access layer — GET /rates queries MongoDB with filters, POST /quote performs stateless computation. No database write operations. Minimal business logic.

findings.title: Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application uses a single hardcoded static API key (ship-2013-abc123-static) checked via x-api-key header middleware. There is no per-caller identity, no OAuth2 client credentials flow, no mTLS, and no principal attribution.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication mechanism exists. A single shared secret provides no caller attribution — impossible to distinguish which agent or service made a request.
findings.recommendation: Replace the static shared API key with an API Gateway authorizer using per-caller API keys or OAuth2 client credentials. Each agent identity should receive a unique credential attributable in access logs.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Replace the static shared API key with an API Gateway authorizer using per-caller API keys or OAuth2 client credentials.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Each agent/service has a unique identity that is attributable in access logs.

findings.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
findings.description: A single shared API key grants identical access to all callers. No mechanism to differentiate access levels — all requests with the valid key can access both GET /rates and POST /quote equally.
findings.gap: No scoped permission model exists. Cannot grant an agent read-only access to /rates without also granting access to /quote.
findings.recommendation: Introduce API Gateway with usage plans that scope each caller to specific endpoints and methods.

compensating_controls: Deploy API Gateway with separate API keys per consumer and resource-level policies
Use service mesh with per-service authorization policies

findings.title: Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. The API key middleware applies uniformly — any valid key holder can call any endpoint with any HTTP method.
findings.gap: Cannot restrict an agent to read operations (GET) while blocking computation (POST) at the authorization layer.
findings.recommendation: Implement method-level authorization — either at API Gateway or as application middleware mapping caller identity to allowed HTTP methods and paths.

compensating_controls: API Gateway method-level authorization with separate policies per HTTP method
Application middleware checking caller identity against allowed-actions list

findings.title: Credential Management
findings.description: API key hardcoded in source: var API_KEY = 'ship-2013-abc123-static'. MongoDB URL hardcoded: var MONGO_URL = 'mongodb://10.0.8.20:27017/shipping'. No secrets management system is used.
findings.gap: Credentials embedded in source code. No rotation capability. Exposure risk via repository access.
findings.recommendation: Refactor application to read credentials from environment variables. Store in AWS Secrets Manager with rotation. K8s deployment already references a Secret — connect the application to consume it.

compensating_controls: Modify application to read from environment variables
Migrate secrets to AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging exists. Only output is console.log('Shipping API listening on 8080'). No request logging, no principal attribution, no immutable storage.
findings.gap: Zero audit trail for API access. Cannot determine who accessed what, when.
findings.recommendation: Add structured request logging middleware with caller attribution. Ship to CloudWatch Logs with retention policy. Configure S3 log archival with Object Lock for immutability.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: agent_scope=read-only, downgraded from conditional BLOCKER
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: AUTH-Q6 resolved as RISK-SAFETY because agent_scope is read-only (inferred from has_write_operations=false). Audit logging remains important but is not a deployment blocker for read-only access.
compensating_controls: Add request-logging middleware with caller identity to CloudWatch Logs
Deploy API Gateway with access logging to immutable S3 destination

findings.title: Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: Single shared API key means no per-agent suspension capability. Revoking access affects all consumers simultaneously.
findings.gap: Cannot isolate a misbehaving agent without disrupting all service consumers.
findings.recommendation: Resolve AUTH-Q1 first (per-caller identity), which naturally enables per-identity suspension via API Gateway key deletion.

compensating_controls: Issue per-agent API keys via API Gateway — individual keys can be disabled
Deploy WAF rule to block specific source IPs as interim measure

findings.title: Compensation and Rollback
findings.description: No compensation or rollback mechanisms exist. The system performs no write operations — GET reads from MongoDB, POST computes a value. No saga patterns or undo endpoints.
findings.gap: No transactional framework exists. Low practical impact given read-only operations.
findings.recommendation: Lower priority given no write operations. Implement saga patterns if write endpoints are added.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to RISK-SAFETY: agent_scope=read-only, downgraded from conditional BLOCKER
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: STATE-Q1 resolved as RISK-SAFETY because agent_scope is read-only (inferred from has_write_operations=false). The system has no multi-step write workflows to compensate.
compensating_controls: Scope agent access to read-only endpoints at API Gateway level
The current read-only nature naturally limits blast radius

findings.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
findings.description: No circuit breakers, retry logic, or timeout configurations for MongoDB dependency. New connection opened per request with no pooling or timeout.
findings.gap: MongoDB failures cascade to all callers with no protection or graceful degradation.
findings.recommendation: Implement MongoDB connection pooling, add timeouts, and introduce circuit breaker pattern (opossum library).

compensating_controls: K8s liveness/readiness probes restart unhealthy pods
Implement connection pooling and timeouts as immediate code changes

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: No rate limiting at any layer. No middleware, no API Gateway, no WAF rules. Express app has no protection against traffic storms.
findings.gap: No protection against agent-driven traffic storms. A runaway agent loop could overwhelm the service.
findings.recommendation: Add express-rate-limit middleware immediately. Deploy API Gateway or NGINX Ingress with throttling for production.

compensating_controls: Add express-rate-limit middleware as immediate code change
Deploy API Gateway or Ingress controller with throttling rules

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, or machine-readable specification found. API endpoints only discoverable by reading source code.
findings.gap: Agent frameworks cannot auto-generate tool definitions from this API.
findings.recommendation: Create an openapi.yaml specification documenting both endpoints with request/response schemas.

compensating_controls: Write OpenAPI spec manually
Use swagger-jsdoc annotations in Express routes

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Error responses are minimal unstructured objects: { error: 'db error' }, { error: 'invalid api key' }. No error codes, no retryable indicators.
findings.gap: Agents cannot distinguish retriable from terminal errors. All failures look the same.
findings.recommendation: Implement consistent error format with error_code, message, and retryable fields.

compensating_controls: Document error strings in agent tool description
Add API Gateway error mapping

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment configuration. No docker-compose, no seed data scripts, no environment-specific configs.
findings.gap: No safe environment to test agent behavior without affecting production.
findings.recommendation: Create docker-compose.yml with MongoDB and seed data for local testing.

compensating_controls: Create docker-compose.yml with MongoDB for local testing
Deploy K8s manifests to separate staging namespace

findings.title: Selective Query Support
findings.description: GET /rates supports origin/dest filtering but has no pagination, sorting, or result size limits. All matching documents returned as full array.
findings.gap: Unbounded result sets possible from broad queries. Agent queries may exhaust LLM context.
findings.recommendation: Add limit/offset parameters with default (100) and maximum (1000) limits.

compensating_controls: Add hardcoded limit to MongoDB find query
Document expected result set sizes in tool definitions

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: No input validation. Query params passed directly to MongoDB filter without sanitization. POST /quote reads weight/zone without type checking. NoSQL injection risk present.
findings.gap: Malformed agent inputs accepted without rejection or structured error feedback.
findings.recommendation: Add validation library (joi/express-validator). Sanitize MongoDB query inputs. Return structured validation errors.

compensating_controls: Add mongo-sanitize middleware for injection prevention
Validate at API Gateway with request validators

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: No temporal metadata in API responses. No timestamps, no Cache-Control headers, no data freshness signaling.
findings.gap: Agents cannot determine when shipping rates were last updated or if data is stale.
findings.recommendation: Add updated_at timestamps to rate documents. Return Cache-Control and Last-Modified headers.

compensating_controls: Add last_updated field to rates collection
Add Cache-Control response headers

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: No API versioning (no /v1/ prefix, no Accept-Version header). No schema documentation, no changelog, no breaking change detection, no contract tests.
findings.gap: Agent tool bindings break silently if API response format changes.
findings.recommendation: Add URL-based versioning (/v1/rates). Document response schemas. Add contract tests.

compensating_controls: Pin agent tool definitions to specific response field expectations
Version URL path before any schema changes

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: No distributed tracing, no structured logging, no correlation IDs. Only a single console.log startup message.
findings.gap: Agent-initiated requests are completely opaque. Cannot diagnose failures.
findings.recommendation: Add pino (structured JSON logger) with request-id middleware. Instrument with OpenTelemetry SDK.

compensating_controls: Add pino with JSON output and request-id middleware
Instrument with OpenTelemetry Node.js SDK

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alerting configuration. No CloudWatch alarms, no monitoring integration, no SLO-based alerting.
findings.gap: Service degradation undetectable until agents report failures.
findings.recommendation: Deploy CloudWatch Container Insights. Configure alarms on 5xx error rate and p99 latency.

compensating_controls: K8s liveness/readiness probes provide basic health detection
Add CloudWatch Container Insights for EKS metrics

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance
findings.description: K8s manifests provide partial IaC (namespace, configmap, deployment, service). No API Gateway, IAM, or networking defined as code. No PR review requirements or drift detection.
findings.gap: Agent-facing integration surface not fully governed as code.
findings.recommendation: Adopt GitOps for K8s manifests. Define API Gateway and IAM as Terraform/CDK.

compensating_controls: Store K8s manifests in GitOps workflow (ArgoCD/Flux)
Add Terraform modules for API Gateway and IAM

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or buildspec.yml. No automated testing or contract testing.
findings.gap: API breaking changes cannot be caught before deployment.
findings.recommendation: Create CI pipeline with Docker build and API contract tests.

compensating_controls: Manual testing against Dockerfile-based build
Add minimal CI workflow with API smoke tests

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: No rollback strategy configured. K8s Deployment uses :latest tag with default RollingUpdate. No blue/green, canary, or automated rollback.
findings.gap: Cannot reliably roll back to previous version if change breaks agent APIs.
findings.recommendation: Pin image tags to specific versions. Configure automated rollback on failed health checks.

compensating_controls: K8s native kubectl rollout undo as manual fallback
Pin image tags for deterministic rollback

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: Zero automated tests. No test framework, no test files, no test dependencies in package.json.
findings.gap: No verification of API behavior for agent consumption.
findings.recommendation: Add jest + supertest integration tests for both endpoints covering valid/invalid inputs and error responses.

compensating_controls: Write minimal Postman/Newman collection
Add mocha/jest with supertest for API tests

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: MongoDB connection uses plaintext (no TLS). No encryption-at-rest configuration. No KMS references. MongoDB has no authentication.
findings.gap: Data at rest and in transit is unencrypted.
findings.recommendation: Enable MongoDB TLS. Enable encryption at rest. Consider migration to Amazon DocumentDB.

compensating_controls: Enable MongoDB TLS and WiredTiger encryption
Migrate to Amazon DocumentDB (encrypted by default)

findings.title: Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: POST /quote performs stateless computation without database writes. No write endpoints exist requiring idempotency controls.
findings.gap: No idempotency mechanism, but none needed for current read-only operations.
findings.recommendation: No action at current scope. Add idempotency keys if write endpoints are introduced.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to INFO: agent_scope=read-only, no write operations exist
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: API-Q4 resolved as INFO because agent_scope is read-only (inferred from has_write_operations=false). POST /quote is pure computation without database writes.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No rate limit documentation. No X-RateLimit-Remaining or Retry-After headers returned. No API Gateway usage plan.
findings.gap: Agents cannot self-throttle based on remaining quota.
findings.recommendation: When rate limiting is implemented (STATE-Q5), include X-RateLimit headers in responses.

findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: No identity propagation. No JWT, no on-behalf-of flows. Archetype calibration: data-gateway serving reference data — identity propagation has minimal security impact.
findings.gap: No caller context propagation, but not a safety concern for reference data.
findings.recommendation: No action required for data-gateway archetype. Reassess if user-specific data introduced.

findings.title: Concurrency Controls
findings.description: No concurrency controls (no optimistic locking, ETags, or version fields). Not applicable for read-only operations.
findings.gap: No write-contention controls, but none needed for read-only scope.
findings.recommendation: No action at read-only scope. Implement optimistic locking if write endpoints introduced.

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No transaction limits. Not applicable for read-only operations — no records modified, no spend triggered.
findings.gap: N/A for read-only scope.
findings.recommendation: No action required. Implement per-caller limits if write endpoints introduced.

findings.title: Draft/Pending State
findings.description: No draft/pending state concept. The application has no state-mutating operations.
findings.gap: N/A for read-only scope.
findings.recommendation: No action required at read-only scope.

findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No approval gates. Not applicable for read-only operations.
findings.gap: N/A for read-only scope.
findings.recommendation: No action required at read-only scope.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: System stores shipping rates (origin, destination, price) — business reference data. No PII, PHI, financial instruments, or credentials in the data store. Stage A = No — not a data-handling target.
findings.gap: N/A — not a sensitive data system.
findings.recommendation: No action required. Monitor for scope creep if customer-specific data introduced.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to INFO: Stage A = No — system stores shipping rates (business reference data), not sensitive data
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q1 resolved as INFO because Stage A determined the system is not a data-handling target. MongoDB stores shipping rates by origin/destination — business reference data without PII, PHI, or financial instruments.

b1.reasoning: Stage A = No, B1 not evaluated

b2.reasoning: Stage A = No, B2 not evaluated

b3.reasoning: Stage A = No, B3 not evaluated

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data quality metrics or monitoring for the shipping rates dataset. No profiling, null rate detection, or freshness SLAs.
findings.gap: Rate data quality is opaque — no completeness or freshness monitoring.
findings.recommendation: Add basic data quality checks for the rates collection.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No data catalog or metadata layer. No AWS Glue catalog, no data dictionary, no schema documentation for MongoDB collections.
findings.gap: Data model must be reverse-engineered from source code.
findings.recommendation: Document MongoDB collection schema in README or separate schema file.

evaluations.title: Documented API Interface
evaluations.reason: Application exposes REST API via Express.js with two HTTP endpoints (GET /rates, POST /quote). Integration is via HTTP.

evaluations.title: Structured Response Format
evaluations.reason: Both endpoints return JSON responses. Express serializes JavaScript objects to JSON by default.

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no operations >30s or long-running workflows detected.

evaluations.title: Event Emission for State Changes
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — data-gateway archetype has no state changes requiring event emission.

evaluations.title: Queryable Current State
evaluations.reason: GET /rates endpoint allows querying current shipping rate state by origin and destination filters.

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — service is not P0 priority and not on critical path.

evaluations.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
evaluations.reason: System stores shipping rate reference data — not subject to GDPR, LGPD, HIPAA, or other data residency regulations. No personal or regulated data.

evaluations.title: PII Redaction in Logs
evaluations.reason: System handles no PII. Data stored is shipping rates. No user-specific data enters the system. Only logging is a startup message.

evaluations.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
evaluations.reason: Field names are human-readable and semantically meaningful: origin, dest, weight, zone, quote. No legacy codes requiring data dictionary.

evaluations.title: Business Outcome Metrics
evaluations.reason: No metrics or telemetry surface exists — informational signal, no finding emitted.

items.summary: Resolve the identity blocker and address critical safety risks: implement per-caller machine identity, scoped permissions, credential management, audit logging, and resilience patterns.
Improve agent integration quality: add API specification, structured errors, input validation, pagination, observability, CI/CD, and encryption.
Address informational items and build long-term maturity: test coverage, documentation, and future-proofing for write-enabled scope expansion.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy centralized identity provider with per-caller credentials
recommended_actions.rationale: Resolves the only BLOCKER and simultaneously addresses 4 RISK-SAFETY findings. Deploy API Gateway with per-caller API keys or OAuth2 client credentials.
Hardcoded credentials in source code are an immediate security risk. K8s manifests already reference secrets — connect the application to consume them.

recommended_actions.action: Add structured logging and audit trail
recommended_actions.rationale: No audit trail and no observability make agent operations completely opaque. Add pino with request-id middleware and ship to CloudWatch.

recommended_actions.action: Implement rate limiting and circuit breakers
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents agent traffic storms from cascading failures. express-rate-limit and opossum can be added with minimal code changes.

recommended_actions.action: Create OpenAPI specification and add input validation
recommended_actions.rationale: Enables agent tool auto-generation and prevents malformed inputs. Foundation for contract testing.
